data.reason: Review round 6 returns on F1 and F2 (medium): the shared-texts ranking and the same-line tie-break can each be deleted with every FindingIdentityTest case green, and SEEN-146 trusts that suite as its regression guard.

findings.claim: The 'more texts shared first' ranking from round 2 is not pinned by any test: removing -shared[pair] from the sort key leaves all 15 FindingIdentityTest cases green, because every fixture that needs it also has the same line or the same id pointing to the right anchor.
findings.failure_scenario: Record 1 holds F1 (high, harness/a.py:1, claim 'It breaks', scenario 'Scenario A') and F2 (low, harness/a.py:5, same claim, scenario 'Scenario B'). Record 2 carries F2 word for word but renamed R1-2 and moved to harness/a.py:6. The code returns {'high': 1, 'low': 1}; with the ranking removed it returns {'low': 2} and every test still passes.
findings.rule_candidate: none: a test that does not isolate one sort criterion is what the mutation-score gate (SEEN-116) measures, not a pattern a static rule can read

findings.claim: The same-line tie-break that note 36 and the second amendment require is not pinned: removing the line comparison leaves all 15 cases green, because the line-tie test keeps line and id pointing to the same anchor.
findings.failure_scenario: Record 1 holds F1 (high, harness/a.py:1, claim 'It breaks', scenario 'Scenario A') and F2 (low, harness/a.py:5, same claim, scenario 'Scenario B'). Record 2 carries F1 at harness/a.py:1 renumbered as F2 with its scenario reworded. The code returns {'high': 1, 'low': 1}; with the line comparison removed it returns {'high': 2} and no test fails.
findings.rule_candidate: none: a fixture where two tie-breaks agree cannot be told from one testing each, which only mutation testing exposes

findings.claim: CLAUDE.md, docs/tickets/README.md and the SEEN-146 ticket file are named by no slice and no changes entry; made on Ruud's decision at note 55.
